tasks.title: Verify the SDK's standalone forkSession against the installed CLIs, and record the result
acceptance: `probe/verify-fork-session.ts` exists and runs with `node probe/verify-fork-session.ts` (the invocation `probe/README.md` documents for the other probes). It calls the standalone `forkSession` exported by `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` as `forkSession(sourceSessionId, { dir: <the source session's cwd> })`, and resumes sessions through the SDK's `query` with `options.resume`, the option the product's resume uses (`src/main/pod/options.ts:238-241`).

The script derives every transcript path with the shipped `sessionFilePath` from `src/main/pod-session/paths.ts`, loaded the way `probe/verify-foreground.ts` loads shipped code (type-only static import plus a URL-based dynamic import), not with a re-implemented path rule.

The script's working directory for the sessions it creates is outside the repository: `PROBE_SCRATCH` when set, otherwise a directory under the OS temp dir, as `probe/README.md` documents for the other probes.

The script runs the whole claim set once against EACH of two CLI binaries, each run with its own freshly created source session: (a) the SDK's built-in executable, which is what the product drives (`src/main/pod/options.ts:243-245` sets `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` only when one is supplied, nothing under `src/` supplies one, and `sdk.d.ts:1775-1777` says the built-in executable is used otherwise; at startRef `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-win32-x64/claude.exe --version` prints `2.1.235 (Claude Code)`); and (b) the `claude` on PATH, passed as `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`.

`probe/evidence/fork-session.json` is written by the script, not by hand, and holds for each binary: that binary's `--version` output; the SDK version read at run time from `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json`; the source and fork session ids; the sha256 of the source transcript at each checkpoint; whether the fork transcript file exists and its byte size at each checkpoint; the nonce; every prompt sent; every assistant reply text; and every `session_id` observed on the resumed fork's messages.

The fact the source session is asked to remember is a nonce generated at random on each run, and no prompt sent to the fork contains it: the nonce string occurs in no fork-side prompt recorded in `probe/evidence/fork-session.json`.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C1 — the id `forkSession` returns differs from the source session id — and, for each binary, the observed ids and a held or refuted verdict, matching `probe/evidence/fork-session.json`.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C2 — a transcript file exists at `sessionFilePath(<claude home>, <cwd>, <fork id>)` once `forkSession` resolves and before any resume — and, for each binary, the observation and a held or refuted verdict, matching the evidence file.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C3 — the source transcript's sha256 is identical immediately before and immediately after `forkSession` — and, for each binary, both hashes and a held or refuted verdict, matching the evidence file.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C4 — a turn sent to the resumed fork asking for the remembered value is answered with the nonce — and, for each binary, the reply text and a held or refuted verdict, matching the evidence file.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C5 — after that turn to the fork, the source transcript's sha256 still equals its pre-fork value — and, for each binary, both hashes and a held or refuted verdict, matching the evidence file.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C6 — every `session_id` carried by the resumed fork's messages equals the fork id, not the source id — and, for each binary, the observed values and a held or refuted verdict, matching the evidence file.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states claim C7 — with the source transcript moved out of its projects directory, a resumed fork still answers with the nonce — and, for each binary, the reply and a held or refuted verdict, plus the source transcript's sha256 after it was moved back, which equals its pre-fork value; the script moves and restores no session file other than the source transcript it created.
`docs/fork-session-verification.md` names the SDK version `0.3.235` and both CLI versions exactly as each binary's `--version` printed them in the evidence file.

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` states an overall verdict, and states the refutation rule: a claim refuted for either binary refutes the documented behaviour for that binary, stops every task that depends on this one, and is raised to the orchestrator as an escalation whose fallback is resuming with the `forkSession: true` query option (`node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1543-1547`).

`docs/fork-session-verification.md` gives the exact command that re-runs the check and the number of live model turns the run spent, counted from the prompts recorded in `probe/evidence/fork-session.json`.

Neither `probe/evidence/fork-session.json` nor `docs/fork-session-verification.md` contains the user's home directory path in any spelling (backslash, forward slash, or the projects-directory encoding `C--Users-dmarq-...`): `rg -c -i -F dmarq <file>` prints nothing (no matching line) for each. (Git Bash `grep -i` aborts with exit 134 in this environment; use `rg`.)

Design doc item 8 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-orcastrate-design.md`, the `Pod branching via forkSession` entry, :458-466 at the base) names the standalone SDK `forkSession(sessionId, { dir })` as the mechanism chosen, states the overall verdict from `docs/fork-session-verification.md`, and links that file by its repository-relative path; no other numbered item of section 10 changes in `git diff` against the task's startRef.
`npm run typecheck` exits 0 (`tsconfig.node.json` includes `probe/**/*`).

tasks.title: Migration 5, Pod ancestry fields, and the store's atomic forkPod
acceptance: `MIGRATIONS` (`src/main/store/schema.ts:713-718`) gains exactly one entry, `version: 5`, appended after version 4, and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 5; the four existing assertions that it is 4 (`tests/unit/store/migration-2.test.ts:55`, `migration-3.test.ts:240`, `migration-4.test.ts:393`, `schema.test.ts:103`) assert 5.

Preserved: the shipped migrations are not edited. `git diff` of `src/main/store/schema.ts` against the task's startRef changes no line of `MIGRATION_1` through `MIGRATION_4` or of the pinned per-migration constants they interpolate (sir database discipline, Migrations: a released migration is never edited).

A database brought to schema version 4 by applying migrations 1-4 and then seeded with at least two pods, their lanes and their events (as `tests/unit/store/migration-4.test.ts` builds its fixture) migrates to version 5 with every pre-existing `pods`, `lanes` and `events` row count and every pre-existing column value unchanged.
On that migrated database both new columns read NULL for every pre-existing pod.
After migration 5, `PRAGMA foreign_key_list(pods)` on a real migrated database reports exactly one foreign key: from `forked_from_pod_id` to `pods(id)`, `on_delete` `SET NULL`.
After migration 5, `PRAGMA table_info(pods)` reports `forked_from_cc_session_id` as a nullable `TEXT` column whose default is NULL.

Encodes database discipline, Naming (keys and constraints are named explicitly): the stored `sqlite_master.sql` for `pods` carries an explicit `CONSTRAINT <name>` on the `forked_from_pod_id` foreign key. (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... CONSTRAINT <name> REFERENCES pods(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` was measured accepted on a STRICT table by the repo's better-sqlite3, SQLite 3.53.4.)
Encodes database discipline, Indexing (every foreign key is indexed): after migration 5, `sqlite_master` holds an index on `pods(forked_from_pod_id)`.

Migration 5's docblock says that `pods` now carries an index, so a future rebuild of `pods` must recreate it — the docblocks of migrations 2 and 3 say `pods` carries no index of its own (`src/main/store/schema.ts:466-470`, `:529-532`), and that stops being true here.
Encodes database discipline, Migrations (every migration is reversible or declares it is not, with the reason): migration 5's docblock declares it not reversible and says why.
Encodes database discipline, Migrations (a migration that changes data is separate from one that changes shape): migration 5's SQL contains no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` statement.

`Pod` in `src/shared/contracts/events.ts` gains `forkedFromPodId: PodId | null` and `forkedFromCcSessionId: string | null`, both required, exactly as `contracts/store-fork.ts` declares, and nothing else on `Pod` changes.
`EventStore.updatePod`'s patch type does not accept either ancestry key: a test passing each one carries `// @ts-expect-error`, and `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
`createPod` returns, and `getPod` and `listPods` read back, both ancestry fields as null.
`EventStore.forkPod` is declared in `src/shared/contracts/event-store.ts` with `ForkPodInput` exactly as `contracts/store-fork.ts` declares, and implemented in `src/main/store/`.
A Pod created by `forkPod` reads back through both `getPod` and `listPods` with `forkedFromPodId` equal to the parent's id and `forkedFromCcSessionId` equal to `input.sourceCcSessionId`.
The `forkPod` row has `ccSessionId` equal to `input.ccSessionId`, `title` equal to `input.title`, `cwd`, `permissionMode` and `envOverrides` equal to the parent's, and `status` `'closed'`.
The `forkPod` row's `tabOrder` is greater than every other pod's, including when existing tabOrders are not dense (pods at 0 and 7 give the fork 8), so it is last in `listPods()`.
The parent's `getPod`, `listLanes` and `readEvents` results deep-equal their values from before `forkPod`.

The fork's `readEvents` equals the parent's events with `seq <= throughSeq`, in order, each with the same `seq`, `type`, `createdAt` and `raw`, `podId` equal to the fork, and `laneId` naming one of the fork's own lanes; no parent event with `seq > throughSeq` is copied.
A copied `lane_opened` event's `payload.lane.id`, `payload.lane.podId` and `payload.lane.parentLaneId` name the fork's lanes and Pod, not the parent's.
A copied `lane_closed` event's `payload.laneId` names the fork's lane, not the parent's.
A copied `tool_use` event carrying `dispatchedLaneId` names the fork's lane, not the parent's.
Every parent lane is copied exactly once with a fresh id from `newLaneId`, and `parentLaneId` is remapped: a depth-2 Calf's copy points at the copy of its depth-1 parent.
A lane `'running'` in the parent is `'stopped'` with `endedAt` equal to `input.now` in the fork, while the parent's lane stays `'running'` with a null `endedAt`.
After `forkPod`, appending one event to the parent leaves the fork's `readEvents` unchanged.
After `forkPod`, appending one event to the fork leaves the parent's `readEvents` unchanged, and that event is assigned `seq` equal to `throughSeq + 1`.
`forkPod` whose `newLaneId` mints an id that collides with an existing lane throws `EventStoreError` `CONFLICT`, and the `pods`, `lanes` and `events` row counts equal their values before the call.
`forkPod` with an `id` that already exists throws `EventStoreError` `CONFLICT`, and the three row counts are unchanged.
`forkPod` with an unknown `parentId` throws `EventStoreError` `NOT_FOUND`, and the three row counts are unchanged.
After `deletePod(parent)`, the fork's row still exists with `forkedFromPodId` null and `forkedFromCcSessionId` unchanged.
After `deletePod(parent)`, the fork's lane count and event count equal their values before the delete.

Every `Pod` literal outside `src/main/store/` that the type change breaks is repaired inside this task's ownership: `makeStubPod` (`src/renderer/src/test-utils/stub-api.ts:117`) defaults both fields to null, and the Pod builders at `tests/unit/ipc/pod-deletion.test.ts:288` and `tests/unit/pod-session/remover.test.ts:34` supply both. Any further site `npm run typecheck` reveals outside the owned paths is reported as an escalation, not edited.

Encodes test discipline, Coverage (a test is shown able to fail): every new test is reported either seen failing before its implementation existed (command and failure named) or failing under a named injected defect at a named file and line, with the injection reverted and the revert verified.
`npm run typecheck` exits 0.
`npm test` exits 0.

tasks.title: PodManager.forkPod over the SDK's forkSession, the pod:fork channel, and the shared eligibility rule
acceptance: `src/shared/fork-eligibility.ts` exports `ForkEligibility` and `forkEligibility` exactly as `contracts/fork-surface.ts` declares.
`forkEligibility` returns `'eligible'` for each of `'closed'`, `'idle'` and `'beached'` with a non-null `ccSessionId`.
`forkEligibility` returns `'mid-turn'` for each of `'running'` and `'waiting'`, with a non-null `ccSessionId` and with a null one.
`forkEligibility` returns `'no-session'` for each of `'closed'`, `'idle'` and `'beached'` with a null `ccSessionId`.
`forkEligibility` fails closed: a status outside `POD_STATUSES` (`src/main/store/schema.ts:40-46`), passed through a cast in a test, returns `'mid-turn'`.
`PodManager.forkPod(podId)` on a `'closed'` parent with a `ccSessionId` calls the fork port exactly once, with the parent's `ccSessionId` and `{ dir: <parent cwd> }`.
The Pod `forkPod` resolves has `ccSessionId` equal to the id the fork port returned, which differs from the parent's.
The Pod `forkPod` resolves has `forkedFromPodId` equal to the parent's id and `forkedFromCcSessionId` equal to the parent's `ccSessionId`.
The Pod `forkPod` resolves has the title `<parent title> (fork)`.
The Pod `forkPod` resolves is `'closed'`, and `createRunner` was not called by the fork.
The parent's `getPod` result deep-equals its value from before `forkPod`.
`forkPod` on a `'running'` parent and on a `'waiting'` parent each rejects with `IpcFailure` `CONFLICT`, does not call the fork port, and leaves the `pods`, `lanes` and `events` row counts unchanged.
`forkPod` on a parent whose `ccSessionId` is null rejects with `IpcFailure` `CONFLICT`, does not call the fork port, and leaves the three row counts unchanged.
`forkPod` whose fork port rejects rejects with `IpcFailure` `IO` and leaves the three row counts unchanged.
Encodes backend discipline, Error handling (include the operation and its inputs in the failure): the `IO` failure's message names the fork operation and the parent PodId.
`forkPod` on an unknown PodId rejects with `NOT_FOUND` and does not call the fork port.
An event appended to the parent while the fork port's promise is still pending is absent from the fork's events: `throughSeq` is captured before the port is awaited.

Encodes database discipline, Transaction scope (nothing that can block on the outside world happens inside a transaction): `store.forkPod` is called only after the fork port's promise has settled, and is never called when it rejects.

Encodes backend discipline, Dependency injection (dependencies are declared in the constructor and immutable thereafter): the fork port is a member of `PodManagerDeps`, held in a readonly field, and every fork test injects a fake rather than reaching the SDK.

`src/main/pod/fork-session.ts` exports the default fork port, which calls the SDK's `forkSession(sourceSessionId, { dir })` and resolves the returned `sessionId` unchanged: a test that mocks `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` observes those exact arguments and that return.
A `PodManager` constructed without a fork port uses the default from `src/main/pod/`, so `src/main/index.ts` needs no change.
After a fork, `manager.openPod(<fork id>)` calls `createRunner` with `resume` equal to the fork's `ccSessionId`, and with neither the parent's `ccSessionId` nor a missing `resume`.
`forkPod` emits no push on any channel.
`INVOKE_CHANNELS.podFork` is `'pod:fork'`, and `registerIpcHandlers` registers it, so its own completeness check (`src/main/ipc/handlers.ts:307-313`) passes.

`pod:fork` invoked through `registerIpcHandlers` with a fake `ipcMain` and a non-string or empty PodId resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and the manager's `forkPod` is not called.
`pod:fork` resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `NOT_FOUND` when the manager rejects with `NOT_FOUND`.
`pod:fork` resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `CONFLICT` when the manager rejects with `CONFLICT`.
`pod:fork` resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `IO` when the fork port rejects.
`pod:fork` resolves `{ ok: true, value }` whose `value` is the forked Pod on success.

The every-handler internal-throw check in `tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts` covers `pod:fork`: its `PodManagerApi` literal (`tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts:141`) gains a throwing `forkPod`, and the channel resolves `{ ok: false }` rather than rejecting.

`window.orcastrate.pods.fork(podId)` invokes `'pod:fork'` with the bare PodId as its only argument, following `open`, `close` and `reconnect` (`src/preload/api.ts:100-103`), shown by a test in `src/preload/api.test.ts`.

`OrcastrateApi['pods']` in `src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts` gains `fork` exactly as `contracts/fork-surface.ts` declares, and `stubOrcastrateApi` (`src/renderer/src/test-utils/stub-api.ts:540`) supplies a default `pods.fork` that a caller can override through its existing overrides argument.

Encodes test discipline, Coverage (a test is shown able to fail): every new test is reported either seen failing before its implementation existed (command and failure named) or failing under a named injected defect at a named file and line, with the injection reverted and the revert verified.
`npm run typecheck` exits 0.

`npm test` exits 0, except for exactly the channel-enumeration tests in T4-owned files that the new `pod:fork` channel fails until T4 adds its action and surface: `src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts` › 'covers every invoke channel between the action table and the lifecycle reads', and `src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx` › 'classifies every channel exactly once…', 'puts the podFork failure on screen if and only if…' and 'covers every channel the sweep found a surface for'; no other test fails.

tasks.title: Fork control on the Pod tab, the forkPod action, and the fork's ancestry on its tab
acceptance: `WorkspaceActions` in `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts` declares `forkPod(podId: PodId): Promise<ActionResult<Pod>>`, documented as resolving and never rejecting, and `ACTION_NAMES` (`src/renderer/src/state/workspace-provider.test.tsx:101`) includes it so the 'exposes every WorkspaceActions method and nothing else' test passes.
On a successful `pods.fork`, the state layer's `forkPod` adds the returned Pod to the Pod list and sets `activePodId` to its id.
On a failed `pods.fork`, the state layer's `forkPod` resolves that failure and leaves the Pod list and `activePodId` unchanged.

Two `forkPod` calls for one PodId while the first is still pending issue exactly one `pods.fork` IPC call (`WorkspaceActions`' docblock, `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts:501-505`, makes the state layer responsible for suppressing an in-flight duplicate).
Every Pod tab renders a Fork control with the accessible name `Fork <title>` for a Pod in each of the five statuses in `POD_STATUSES` (`src/main/store/schema.ts:40-46`).
Activating the Fork control on a `'closed'` Pod with a `ccSessionId`, through the real state layer and a stub API, calls `pods.fork` exactly once, with that Pod's id.
After a successful fork, the returned Pod's tab is rendered in the last position of the Pod bar.
After a successful fork, the returned Pod's tab is the active tab (`aria-current="true"`).
Encodes frontend discipline, Accessibility floor (focus moves predictably after an action that changes what is on screen): after a successful fork, keyboard focus is on the new Pod's tab button.

For a Pod whose `forkEligibility` is `'no-session'`, the Fork control has `aria-disabled="true"` and an accessible description saying there is no conversation to fork yet, and activating it by click and by Enter makes no `pods.fork` call.

For a `'running'` and for a `'waiting'` Pod, the Fork control has `aria-disabled="true"` and an accessible description saying the Pod is mid-turn, and activating it by click and by Enter makes no `pods.fork` call.

Encodes frontend discipline, Accessibility floor (every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard alone): the ineligible Fork control carries no `disabled` attribute and is reached by Tab, so its stated reason is reachable by keyboard; the eligible control forks on Enter and on Space.

The renderer decides eligibility only by calling `forkEligibility` from `src/shared/fork-eligibility.ts`, per `contracts/fork-surface.ts` (one implementation, two consumers): no file under `src/renderer/src/pods/` compares a status to `'running'` or `'waiting'` to decide whether to offer a fork.
Encodes frontend discipline, Data fetching (every fetch has a declared loading state): while a fork is in flight, that tab's Fork control reports `aria-busy="true"`.

Encodes frontend discipline, Data fetching (every fetch has a declared error state): when `pods.fork` resolves `{ ok: false }`, main's message is shown verbatim in an element with `role="alert"` and no tab is added.
A tab whose Pod's `forkedFromPodId` names a listed Pod has an accessible description containing `Forked from <that Pod's title>`.
A tab whose Pod has `forkedFromPodId` null and `forkedFromCcSessionId` non-null has an accessible description saying it was forked from a deleted Pod.
A tab whose Pod has both ancestry fields null carries no `Forked from` text.

Encodes frontend discipline, State ownership (derived values are computed, never stored): after the parent Pod is renamed through `updatePod`, the fork's tab description names the new title with no further action.

The Fork control's glyph rides an `aria-hidden` span with `data-icon="fork"`, the convention `src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.tsx:11-18` sets for the tab's other controls, so colour is not its only carrier.

The existing test pinning a closed Pod's tab to exactly two controls (`src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.test.tsx:113`) is revised to include the Fork control, and still asserts the run and delete controls it asserted before.

Encodes the Orcastrate frontend fragment, Indexed access under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`: no line this task adds uses a non-null assertion `!` or an `as` cast to guard an indexed or destructured value.

Encodes test discipline, Coverage (a test is shown able to fail): every new test is reported either seen failing before its implementation existed (command and failure named) or failing under a named injected defect at a named file and line, with the injection reverted and the revert verified.
Repo-wide `npm run typecheck` exits 0 at this task's tip, the DAG tail (vitest does not typecheck).
Repo-wide `npm test` exits 0 at this task's tip, the DAG tail.
